newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS keeps forecast at 3.80 pct for Swiss 10-yr bond.
newsitem.headline: CS keeps forecast at 3.80 pct for Swiss 10-yr bond.

text.p: In its latest market report, Credit Suisse Research said it was leaving its monthly forecast for Swiss 10-year federal bond yields at 3.80 percent.
The forecast was roughly 20 basis points below the level of the benchmark June 2007 bond 0#CH470458= on Tuesday.

CS said an increase in base money growth in Switzerland this year has not fed into inflationary expectations, and a weak economic outlook also makes an upward correction in long-term interest rates look unlikely.
Swiss National Bank chief economist Georg Rich said last week that real growth in Switzerland in 1997 could be below 1.0 percent.
CS also does not expect any "major changes" in the mark bond market for the near term.
"We are therefore leaving our one-month forecast for the 10-year benchmark bond unchanged at 3.8 percent," CS analyst Kim Blaser wrote in the bank's latest weekly bond letter.
CS said the forecast also "represents a slight increase in the spread" between 10-year Swiss and German federal bonds.
CS noted that the yield spread between 10-year Swiss and German bonds had continued to narrow, dipping to 164 basis points last week.

"Since the Deutschemark bond market performed significantly better, the yield spread to Germany fell to 164 basis points. The last time we saw such a low spread was at the beginning of the year," CS said.
The spread was at 168 basis points on Tuesday YLDS3.

It said that the recent narrowing of the German/Swiss bond yield spread by about 30 basis points probably had more to do with "a mood of confidence regarding monetary union, and less to do with changes in the mark/Swiss exchange rate."
The spread has been as wide as about 240 basis points, and as narrow as about 140 this year, analysts said.
CS said the spread has fluctuated around 200 basis points during the 1990s.
